# Built-in functions and procedures

The builtins every runtime implements (native builds, the interpreter and the web share one list, unit-tested against each runtime's dispatch). Names are not case-sensitive, and a builtin may be written with or without its type suffix: `MID$`, `Mid` and `mid` are the same. *bare*: may be written without parentheses or arguments (`t = TIMER`); *(RapidR)*: RapidQ doesn't have it; *not yet*: RapidQ's, not in RapidR yet. Statements are in [statements.md](statements.md).

## Arrays and memory

| Builtin | |
|---|---|
| `INITARRAY(Array, values, ...)` *(not yet)* | Fills an array with the values listed, from its first element on. |
| `LBOUND(ArrayName[, Dimension])` | The lowest index of an array, in its first dimension or the one given (1 the first). |
| `MEMCMP(ptr1, ptr2, count)` | Compares `count` bytes at two addresses: true (-1) when they are the same, 0 when not (unlike C's memcmp). |
| `MEMCPY(dest, source, count)` | Copies `count` bytes from one address to another (addresses from `VARPTR`, `UDTPTR` or a stream's `Pointer`); in RapidR a bad address is a run-time error, never a crash. |
| `MEMSET(ptr, byte, count)` | Sets `count` bytes from an address to one byte value. |
| `PEEK([#PageNum,] address)` | Reads one byte: of a console page (addresses 0 to 3999 of page 0 are the screen, an even address a cell's character, the odd one after it its colour attribute), or of the program's own memory at an address from VARPTR and the like. Any other address is a run-time error. |
| `POKE [#PageNum,] address, byte` | Writes one byte: into a console page (on page 0 it shows at once), or into the program's own memory at an address from VARPTR and the like. Any other address is a run-time error. |
| `SIZEOF (Var(Index))` | The size in bytes of a variable, array element, array, type or TYPE, as RapidQ lays it out in memory. |
| `UBOUND(ArrayName[, Dimension])` | The highest index of an array, in its first dimension or the one given (1 the first). |
| `UDTPTR(Variable)` | The address of a TYPE variable's fields, for `MEMCPY` and the other memory builtins. |
| `VARPTR(VarName)` | The address of a variable or array element, for the memory builtins; in RapidR a safe view of the program's own data. |

## Colours

| Builtin | |
|---|---|
| `RGB(Red%, Green%, Blue%)` | The colour value for red, green and blue parts of 0 to 255 each, as RapidQ stores colours (blue in the high byte). |

## Console

| Builtin | |
|---|---|
| `CLS` | Clears the console and moves the cursor to the top left corner. |
| `COLOR [Fore%][, Back%]` | Sets the console's text colours: foreground 0 to 15, background 0 to 7, in the classic 16-colour palette; without arguments, the terminal's own colours. |
| `CSRLIN` *bare* | The console cursor's row, 1 being the top. |
| `INKEY$` *bare* | The next key pressed, or "" when none is waiting; it doesn't wait. Special keys (arrows, F1–F12, …) come as `CHR$(27)` followed by their scan code. |
| `INPUT$(NumChars)` | Waits for `NumChars` keys to be pressed and returns them as a string. |
| `ISCONSOLE` *(not yet)* | True when the program is running as a console program. |
| `LOCATE [Y%][, X%][, cursor]` | Moves the console cursor to row `Y`, column `X` (1 the first); a value left out keeps the current one. |
| `PCOPY source, dest` | Copies one console page (0 is the screen, 1 to 7 are off-screen buffers) onto another. |
| `POS(0)` | The console cursor's column, 1 being the first. |
| `SETCONSOLETITLE(Title$)` | Sets the title of the console (terminal) window. |
| `TAB(Column)` | In `PRINT`: spaces up to console column `Column` (1 the first); past it already, that column on the next line. |

## Dialogs and sound

| Builtin | |
|---|---|
| `BEEP` *(RapidR)* | Plays a short beep on the system's sound output (without sound, the terminal's bell). |
| `MESSAGEBOX(Msg$, Title$, MsgButtons%)` | Shows a message box with the buttons and icon the `MB_` flags ask for; returns the `ID` constant (`IDOK`, `IDYES`, …) of the button chosen. |
| `MESSAGEDLG(Msg$, MsgType, MsgButtons, HelpContext)` | Shows a message dialog of a type (`mtWarning`, `mtError`, `mtInformation`, `mtConfirmation`, `mtCustom`) with the `mb` buttons given; returns the `mr` constant of the one chosen. |
| `MSGBOX(Msg$)` *(RapidR)* | Shows a message box with an OK button and returns 0 when it is closed. |
| `PLAYSOUND(FileName$)` *(RapidR)* | Plays a sound file in the background. |
| `PLAYWAV FileName$\|Resource_Handle, SndOption` | Plays a WAV file or `$RESOURCE` in the background (`SND_ASYNC`), waiting for its end (`SND_SYNC`) or repeating (`SND_LOOP`); `PLAYWAV ""` stops it. |
| `SHOWMESSAGE text$` | Shows a message in a modal box with an OK button, titled with the application's title. |
| `SOUND freq, duration` | Plays a tone of a frequency in hertz for a duration in milliseconds, in the background. |

## Files and folders

| Builtin | |
|---|---|
| `CHDIR path$` | Makes a folder the current one, the folder relative paths start from. |
| `CHDRIVE "a:\"` | Makes a drive (`"d:"`) the current one on Windows; other systems have no drives and it does nothing. |
| `CLOSE #FileNum` *(RapidR)* | Closes the file opened with `OPEN` under that number; what was written to it is kept. |
| `CURDIR$` *bare* | The full path of the current folder. |
| `DIR$[(FileSpec$, Attributes%)]` *bare* | The first file matching a pattern with `*` and `?` (any case), or "" when none; then bare `DIR$` gives the next. Attributes: faDirectory includes folders, faHidden hidden files. |
| `DIREXISTS(Path$)` | True (1) when a folder of that path exists, else 0. |
| `EOF(FileNum)` *(RapidR)* | True (-1) when a file opened with `OPEN` has nothing left to read (or isn't open), else 0. |
| `EXTRACTRESOURCE ResourceNumber%, FileName$` | Writes a resource built into the program (`$RESOURCE`, its handle from `RESOURCE(n)`) to a file. |
| `FILEEXISTS(FileName$)` | True (1) when a file of that name exists, else 0 (a folder doesn't count). |
| `FILELEN(FileName$)` *(RapidR)* | The size of a file in bytes, 0 when it doesn't exist. |
| `FREEFILE` *(RapidR)* *bare* | The lowest file number not in use, for `OPEN … AS #n`. |
| `KILL Filename$` | Deletes a file. |
| `LOF(FileNum)` *(RapidR)* | The length in bytes of a file opened with `OPEN`. |
| `MKDIR Dir$` | Creates a folder. |
| `OPEN FileName$ FOR mode AS #FileNum` *(RapidR)* | Opens a file for `INPUT`, `OUTPUT`, `APPEND`, `BINARY` or `RANDOM` access under a file number (see `FREEFILE`). |
| `RENAME File1$, File2$` | Renames (or moves) a file from the first name to the second. |
| `RESOURCE(number%)` | The handle of the n-th resource built into the program with `$RESOURCE` (0 the first), for `EXTRACTRESOURCE`, `PLAYWAV` or a picture. |
| `RESOURCECOUNT` *bare* | The number of resources built into the program with `$RESOURCE`. |
| `RMDIR Dir$` | Removes an empty folder. |
| `SEEK #FileNum, Position` *(RapidR)* | Moves to a byte of a file opened with `OPEN`: the next read or write is there (1 the first byte). |

## Library functions

RapidQ programs get these from include files or DECLAREs (RapidQ's compiler doesn't know them itself); RapidR doesn't have them yet.

| Builtin | |
|---|---|
| `CONVBASEX(Str$, FromBase, ToBase)` *(not yet)* | A variant of `CONVBASE$` for converting a string of digits from one number base to another. |
| `Execute function` *(not yet)* | Runs a routine named by a string at run time. |
| `GETCAPTURE` *(not yet)* | The handle of the window that has captured the mouse, 0 if none. |
| `GETFOCUS` *(not yet)* | The handle of the window that has the keyboard focus. |
| `MICROTIMER` *(not yet)* | A high-resolution timer reading, for timing short intervals more finely than `TIMER`. |
| `NVIEWLIBPRESENT` *(not yet)* | Whether the NViewLib image library (JPEG and other formats) is available to the program. |
| `RELEASECAPTURE` *(not yet)* | Releases the mouse capture a window holds. |
| `RTLMOVEMEMORY(dest, source, count)` *(not yet)* | Copies a block of memory from one address to another (Windows' routine of that name). |
| `SETCAPTURE(Handle)` *(not yet)* | Makes a window receive all mouse input until the capture is released. |
| `SETFOCUS(Handle)` *(not yet)* | Gives the keyboard focus to a window by its handle. |
| `WSTRING(String$)` *(not yet)* | A string converted to wide (UTF-16) characters, for routines that take Unicode text. |
| `WSTRINGTOASCII(WideString)` *(not yet)* | A wide (UTF-16) string converted back to an ordinary one. |

## Numbers

| Builtin | |
|---|---|
| `ABS(Number)` | The absolute value of a number; an integer stays an integer. |
| `ACOS(Number)` | The arc cosine of a number from -1 to 1, as an angle in radians (0 to π). |
| `ASIN(Number)` | The arc sine of a number from -1 to 1, as an angle in radians (-π/2 to π/2). |
| `ATAN(Number)` | The arc tangent of a number, in radians; the same as `ATN`. |
| `ATN(Number)` | The arc tangent of a number, as an angle in radians (-π/2 to π/2). |
| `CBOOL(Expression)` | A value as a truth value: true for a non-zero number, or for a text that is a non-zero number or (not a number) isn't empty; false otherwise. |
| `CDBL(Expression)` *(RapidR)* | A value as a DOUBLE (a text is read as `VAL` reads it). |
| `CEIL(Number)` | The smallest whole number not less than a number (`CEIL(2.1)` is 3, `CEIL(-2.1)` -2), as a 32-bit integer. |
| `CINT(Number)` | A number rounded to an integer as `INT(x + 0.5)`: 2.5 gives 3, -2.5 gives -2. Beyond 32 bits, -2147483648. |
| `CLNG(Number)` | A number rounded to a 32-bit integer, as `CINT` rounds it: `INT(x + 0.5)`. |
| `COS(Number)` | The cosine of an angle in radians. |
| `CSNG(Expression)` *(RapidR)* | A value as a SINGLE (a text is read as `VAL` reads it). |
| `EXP(Number)` | e raised to the power of a number; the inverse of `LOG`. |
| `FIX(Number)` | A number's whole part, truncated toward zero (`FIX(-2.7)` is -2); the same as `INT` in RapidQ. |
| `FLOOR(Number)` | The largest whole number not greater than a number (`FLOOR(-2.1)` is -3), as a 32-bit integer. |
| `FRAC(Number)` | A number's fractional part, with its sign: `FRAC(-2.75)` is -0.75. |
| `IIF(Condition, TrueValue, FalseValue)` | `TrueValue` when the condition is true, else `FalseValue`. Both are evaluated before the choice. |
| `INT(Number)` | A number's whole part, truncated toward zero as RapidQ does (`INT(-2.5)` is -2), kept as large as the number. |
| `INV(Number, Modulus)` | The modular inverse of a number (`INV(3, 26)` is 9), or -1 when there is none; also an operator, `a INV m`. |
| `LOG(Number)` | The natural logarithm (base e) of a positive number. |
| `PI` *(RapidR)* *bare* | The number π, 3.14159265358979… |
| `RANDOMIZE [Num]` | Starts `RND`'s sequence from a seed: the same seed gives the same numbers on every runtime. Without one, a fresh seed. |
| `RND(UpperBound)` *bare* | A random number: bare, a real from 0 up to (not including) 1; `RND(n)`, a whole number from 0 to n - 1. `RANDOMIZE` seeds it. |
| `ROUND(Number)` | A number rounded as `INT(x + 0.5)`: 2.5 gives 3, -2.5 gives -2; a 32-bit integer. |
| `SGN(Number)` | The sign of a number: 1 if positive, -1 if negative, 0 if zero. |
| `SHL(Number, Bits)` | A number's 32 bits shifted left by `Bits` (its low 5 bits), as a signed 32-bit integer; also an operator, `a SHL n`. |
| `SHR(Number, Bits)` | A number's 32 bits shifted right by `Bits` (its low 5 bits), zeros coming in from the left; also an operator, `a SHR n`. |
| `SIN(Number)` | The sine of an angle in radians. |
| `SQR(Number)` | The square root of a number. |
| `TAN(Number)` | The tangent of an angle in radians. |
| `VARTYPE(variant)` | A code for the kind of value a VARIANT holds, as VB numbers them: 0 empty, 2 integer, 5 double, 8 string, 9 object, 11 Boolean. |

## Other

| Builtin | |
|---|---|
| `GET$(NumChars)` | Reads up to `NumChars` bytes from standard input as they are (for a CGI program, its request body); "" at the end. |

## Routines

| Builtin | |
|---|---|
| `CALLBACK(MySub)` *(not yet)* | The address of a SUB or FUNCTION, in the form a Windows API routine needs to call it back (a window procedure, an enumeration callback). |
| `CALLFUNC(Num, param1, param2, ...)` | Calls the SUB or FUNCTION a pointer holds (from `BIND` or `CODEPTR`) with the arguments given; returns a FUNCTION's result. |
| `CODEPTR(MySub)` *(not yet)* | The address of a SUB or FUNCTION, for `CALLFUNC` or a routine that takes a pointer to call. |
| `PARAMSTR$(n)` | In a `SUBI` or `FUNCTIONI`: the n-th string argument it was called with (1 the first), "" past the last. |
| `PARAMSTRCOUNT` | In a `SUBI` or `FUNCTIONI`: how many string arguments it was called with. |
| `PARAMVAL(n)` | In a `SUBI` or `FUNCTIONI`: the n-th numeric argument it was called with (1 the first), 0 past the last. |
| `PARAMVALCOUNT` | In a `SUBI` or `FUNCTIONI`: how many numeric arguments it was called with. |

## Strings

| Builtin | |
|---|---|
| `ASC(char$)` | The character code of a string's first character, 0 for an empty string; the inverse of `CHR$`. It counts characters, not UTF-8 bytes: `ASC("é")` is 233. |
| `BIN$(Integer)` | The binary digits of a number's 32 bits, without leading zeros: `BIN$(5)` is `101`, `BIN$(-1)` is 32 ones. A real number is rounded to a whole one first. |
| `CHR$(byte)` | The one-character string whose code is the number's low byte (`CHR$(65)` is `A`); a real number is rounded half to even first. |
| `CONVBASE$(Str$, FromBase, ToBase)` | A number written in one base (2 to 36) as a string of digits in another: `CONVBASE$("FF", 16, 10)` is `255`. A negative number converts as its 32 bits; "" for a bad base or digit. |
| `DELETE$(String$, Index, Count)` | The string with `Count` characters removed starting at position `Index` (1 the first): `DELETE$("Hello", 2, 3)` is `Ho`. |
| `FIELD$(StringExpresion, Deliminator, FieldNumber)` | The n-th piece (1 the first) of a string split at every occurrence of a separator: `FIELD$("a,b,c", ",", 2)` is `b`; "" out of range. |
| `FORMAT$(S$, arg1, arg2, ...)` | Text built from a pattern and values, Pascal style: `%d`, `%s`, `%f`, `%x`, `%e`, `%g`, `%n`, `%m` with optional width and precision: `FORMAT$("%5.2f", 3.14159)` is ` 3.14`. |
| `HEX$(Number)` | The hexadecimal digits of a number's 32 bits, always 8 of them: `HEX$(255)` is `000000FF`. A real number is rounded half to even first. |
| `HEXTODEC(Hex$)` | The number a string of hexadecimal digits stands for (`&H` or `0x` in front allowed): `HEXTODEC("FF")` is 255; 0 when it isn't hexadecimal. |
| `INSERT$(Source$,Dest$,Index)` | `Dest$` with `Source$` inserted before character `Index` (1 the first): `INSERT$("hi", "Hello", 3)` is `Hehillo`. |
| `INSTR([Start,] Search$,Find$)` | The position (1 the first) where `Find$` first occurs in `Search$`, from character `Start` when given; 0 when it doesn't (an empty `Find$` is never found). |
| `ISNUMERIC(Expression)` *(RapidR)* | True (-1) when the value is a number or a text that is exactly a number (`"3.5"`, `"-2E3"`), else 0. |
| `LCASE$(String)` | The string in lower case. |
| `LEFT$(String,Num)` | The first `Num` characters of a string (all of it when it is shorter). |
| `LEN(String)` | The number of characters in a string (characters, not bytes). |
| `LTRIM$(String)` | The string without its leading spaces. |
| `MID$(String, Position, Num)` | `Num` characters of a string from `Position` (1 the first); without `Num`, the rest of the string. |
| `OCT(Number)` *(RapidR)* | The octal digits of a whole number, as text: `OCT(8)` is `10`. |
| `REPLACE$(Source$, Replace$, Index)` | `Replace$` written over `Source$` from character `Index` (1 the first): `REPLACE$("Hello", "J", 1)` is `Jello`. To find and replace, `REPLACESUBSTR$`. |
| `REPLACESUBSTR$(Source$, ReplaceStr$, Withstr$)` | `Source$` with every occurrence of `ReplaceStr$` replaced by `Withstr$`. |
| `REVERSE$(S$)` | The string with its characters in reverse order. |
| `RIGHT$(String,Num)` | The last `Num` characters of a string (all of it when it is shorter). |
| `RINSTR([Start,] SearchString, FindString)` | The position (1 the first) of the last occurrence of `FindString` in `SearchString`, 0 when there is none. |
| `RTRIM$(String)` | The string without its trailing spaces. |
| `SPACE$(Num)` | A string of `Num` spaces. |
| `STR$(Number)` | A number as text, with up to 9 significant digits as RapidQ writes it: `STR$(1 / 3)` is `0.333333333`. |
| `STRF$(Number, Format%, Precision%, Digits%)` | A number as text in a float format (`ffGeneral`, `ffExponent`, `ffFixed`, `ffNumber`) with `Precision%` significant digits and `Digits%` decimals. |
| `STRING$(Num, Char) or STRING$(Num, Char$)` | A string of `Num` copies of a character, given by its code or as the first character of a string: `STRING$(3, 65)` is `AAA`. |
| `TALLY(Search$, Match$)` | The number of times `Match$` occurs in `Search$` (occurrences don't overlap); 0 for an empty `Match$`. |
| `TRIM(String)` *(RapidR)* | The string without its leading and trailing spaces. |
| `UCASE$(String)` | The string in upper case. |
| `VAL(String)` | The number at the start of a text, ignoring spaces and what follows it: `VAL("12abc")` is 12; 0 when there is none. |

## System

| Builtin | |
|---|---|
| `COMMAND$[(n)]` *bare* | The program's command line: `COMMAND$(n)` the n-th argument (`COMMAND$(0)` the program itself, "" past the last); bare, the arguments together. |
| `COMMANDCOUNT` *bare* | The number of arguments on the program's command line (not counting the program itself); COMMAND$(n) reads each. |
| `DATE$` *bare* | Today's local date as text, `MM-DD-YYYY`. |
| `DOEVENTS` | Lets pending window events, timers and repaints run, so a long loop keeps the program's windows responsive. |
| `ENVIRON StringExpression` | `ENVIRON "NAME=value"` sets a variable in the program's environment; `ENVIRON$("NAME")` reads one ("" when unset). |
| `INP(Address)` | Reads a byte from a hardware I/O port. Windows doesn't let programs reach the ports, so the call stops the program with a run-time error, as it did under RapidQ on Windows. |
| `INPW(Address)` | Reads a 16-bit word from a hardware I/O port. Windows doesn't let programs reach the ports, so the call stops the program with a run-time error. |
| `KILLMESSAGE hWnd, Message` *(not yet)* | Removes pending messages of one kind from a window's message queue. |
| `LFLUSH` | Sends what `LPRINT` has printed so far to the printer as one job; what is left at the program's end is printed then. |
| `LIBRARYINST(DLLName)` *(not yet)* | Loads a DLL and returns its instance handle, 0 when it can't be loaded: a way to test whether a library is present. |
| `LPRINT [Expression][;\|,][...]` | Prints to the printer as `PRINT` prints to the console; `LFLUSH` sends the job. RapidR makes each job a PDF for the system's printer. |
| `MOUSEX` *bare* | The mouse pointer's horizontal position, relative to the active form's client area. |
| `MOUSEY` *bare* | The mouse pointer's vertical position, relative to the active form's client area. |
| `OUT(Address, bytevalue)` | Writes a byte to a hardware I/O port. Windows doesn't let programs reach the ports, so the call stops the program with a run-time error, as it did under RapidQ on Windows. |
| `OUTW(Address, wordvalue)` | Writes a 16-bit word to a hardware I/O port. Windows doesn't let programs reach the ports, so the call stops the program with a run-time error. |
| `POSTMESSAGE(Handle, uMsg, wParam, lParam)` *(not yet)* | Puts a Windows message in a window's queue and returns without waiting for it to be handled. |
| `RUN command$` | Starts a program (a command line) without waiting for it; returns its process ID, 0 when it couldn't start. |
| `SENDMESSAGE(Handle, uMsg, wParam, lParam)` *(not yet)* | Sends a Windows message to a window and waits for the result its window procedure returns. |
| `SHELL command$` | Runs a command with the system's shell and waits until it has finished; returns its exit code. |
| `SHELLWAIT(command$)` *(RapidR)* | Runs a command with the system's shell, waits until it has finished and returns its exit code (-1 when it couldn't run). |
| `SLEEP Num` | Pauses the program for a number of seconds; fractions allowed (`SLEEP 0.5`). |
| `TIME$` *bare* | The local time as text, `HH:MM:SS`. |
| `TIMER` *bare* | The seconds since midnight (local time), with fractions, for timing parts of a program. |
| `UNLOADLIBRARY(DLLName)` *(not yet)* | Unloads a DLL the program loaded. |

158 builtins.
